A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIT-GNN. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification and regression experiments, inference-time and memory measurements, and ablations for FIT-GNN.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds training/inference controls, label-variation measurements, and neighborhood-loss analyses in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a described inference adaptation for an arriving test node: assign it to a subgraph using its neighboring nodes, append Extra/Cluster Nodes, and infer locally. This extension is analyzed theoretically, without reported experimental validation. The core partitioning, augmentation, losses, and training algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 13 datasets for node and graph classification and regression. Appendix G reuses existing datasets. QM9's numbered targets are relabeled with property symbols, and the new-node scenario is analyzed theoretically rather than experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a subgraph-trained, full-graph-inferred GCN control to the comparison with full-graph GCN and FIT-GNN. The established benchmark comparator families, including SGGC, GCOND, BONSAI, DOSCOND, and KIDD, remain. The two-hop inference alternative receives only a theoretical comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E changes the stated training budget from 300 to 20 epochs, a substantial revision to the reported experimental settings. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. Appendix G also introduces crossed training/inference controls and label-variation and neighborhood-loss measurements, with r = 0.5 specified for the latter.

E4.justification: New Appendix G investigates previously untested explanations for the regression advantage through training-versus-inference controls, global-versus-local label variation, and two-hop neighborhood-loss histograms across four datasets. Existing Cora and coarsening-method ablations are retained; moving the Cora plot into the main text does not add an experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain reporting of means and standard deviations for the top 10 accuracies and lowest 10 MAEs. No new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented. Appendix G's label standard deviations measure data variation, not uncertainty in model performance.

E6.justification: The OGBN-Products Full reference changes from 0.873 ± 0.000 in v4 Table 5 to 0.823 ± 0.001 in v5 Table 3; FIT-GNN remains 0.894 ± 0.000. Different splits remain disclosed, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation. Appendix G adds diagnostic results, including the 0.865 MAE crossed control, label-variation statistics, and neighborhood-loss distributions. Other existing benchmark, timing, memory, and coarsening results match.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds preprocessing and arriving-node complexity comparisons in Tables 9 and 10. Section 3 also changes the adjacency definition to allow real-valued weights and specifies k = floor(nr). The existing lemmas, corollary, and substantive proof arguments are retained, with explanatory and notational edits.

C1.justification: The introduction changes its description of the theoretical contribution from an upper bound on the coarsening ratio to one on expected subgraph size, aligning it with the existing lemma. The abstract, numbered contributions, and principal speed, memory, and competitive-performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explains node-regression behavior mainly through information loss as subgraphs shrink. v5 develops a substantially different explanation for the regression advantage: inference locality, lower local label variation, and implicit pruning of noisy long-range information. It also adds interpretations concerning preprocessing-inclusive efficiency and arriving-node inference, and revises the molecular explanation from positional-information loss to individual-node-information loss.

D1.justification: Appendix E revises the documented epoch count from 300 to 20. Optimizer settings, two GCN layers, 512 hidden dimensions, and hardware specifications remain unchanged. Appendix G supplies settings for its new diagnostics. The source-code link has the same destination despite its revised display.

R1.justification: v5 adds Luo et al. (2024) as the source of the OGBN-Products Full result and explains the exclusion of Cluster-GCN experiments in Appendix F. Most other reference changes update bibliographic details for already-cited works rather than introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 makes targeted prose and pseudocode edits, collapses the preliminary subsections into inline headings, reorders the classification/regression discussion, and adds appendix subsections and an acknowledgment. Author-credit and publication-header text also change. The overall narrative structure and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and the Cora ablation moves from v4 Figure 5 in the appendix to v5 Figure 3 in the main text. New complexity and diagnostic Tables 9, 10, 16, and 17 and Figure 7 substantially expand the displays. Existing tables are rearranged and relabeled, including clearer QM9 target headings; retained experimental plots preserve their image content.

improvement.justification: Appendix G provides useful controls for the previously unexplained regression advantage, while Appendix C.2 broadens cost accounting and the revised attribution makes the OGBN reference more traceable. These improve explanation and assessability. The gains are limited: the pruning mechanism is not causally established, and the change from 300 to 20 epochs is not reconciled with the retained result values.
